item.title: Ranking England's Ballon d'Or winners - how does Kane compare?
item.description: [BBC] English Ballon d'Or winners have been few and far between. Triumphs to be treasured, names never to be forgotten. Harry Kane, England's great talisman and captain, is the first to claim football's grandest individual accolade in 25 years after a sensational campaign in Bayern Munich colours - and only the fifth Englishman to ever do so. Before him Michael Owen, in 2001, was the first Three Lions star to take it since Kevin Keegan's successive triumphs 22 years earlier. England World Cup winner Bobby Charlton did it in 1966, and that came after Stanley Matthews won the inaugural prize a decade earlier - handed what began life as the European Footballer of the Year award in 1956. Others have come close - Billy Wright, Bobby Moore, Gary Lineker, David Beckham and Frank Lampard are all among the runners-up. Lucy Bronze, in 2019, and Beth Mead, 2022, also more recently finished second. Of course, the award has gradually evolved into the global behemoth it is today. The caveat with those earlier winners is that it was not a worldwide prize - until 1995 it was only open to European players, and only in 2007 did it expand to include all players from all clubs across the world. However, that does not detract from the award-winning performances these stars produced - each enjoyed prize-worthy campaigns that caught voters' eyes across Europe and the world. But who among the five to have held the coveted prize is England's greatest Ballon d'Or winner? 5. Michael Owen, Liverpool, 2001 Only Brazil's Ronaldo, in 1997, was younger than Owen when he won the Ballon d'Or in 2001 [Getty Images] We won't hold it against Michael Owen for suggesting he didn't know what the Ballon d'Or was when Gerard Houllier first rang to announce he'd won it. And, in fairness, the then 22-year-old swotted up sufficiently by the time he received the award, reeling off a list of previous winners. Owen in those days, even after his initial hamstring struggles, was explosive, electric - searing pace and acceleration complemented by the most ruthless of finishes. He became a renowned goalscorer in his teenage years and, by 2001, was one of the most sought-after youngsters in world football. Owen's Ballon d'Or-winning year was one of iconic moments. He helped Liverpool to a treble, clinching the League Cup on penalties before beating Arsenal in the FA Cup final - Owen scored twice late on to turn the game in Liverpool's favour. The leveller was an acrobatic and clinically taken strike inside the Arsenal box, the winner a devastating break in which the prolific striker darted away from Lee Dixon and Tony Adams before slotting past David Seaman with his left foot. The forward then set up two of the goals as Houllier's side beat Alaves 5-4 in extra time in the Uefa Cup final, having earlier in the competition scored a famous double against Roma at the Stadio Olimpico that carried the Reds through. item.title: France Football chief reveals how close Kylian Mbappe came to winning 2026 Ballon d’Or: ‘Was leading for a long time’
item.description: France Football chief reveals how close Kylian Mbappe came to winning 2026 Ballon d’Or: ‘Was leading for a long time’ Real Madrid superstar Kylian Mbappe enjoyed an extraordinary 2025-26 campaign, scoring 42 goals for his club and another ten at the World Cup. His performances made him one of the leading contenders for the Ballon d’Or, but it eventually went to Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane . As quoted by AS , France Football editor-in-chief Vincent Garcia has now revealed just how close Mbappe came to winning his first-ever Ballon d’Or. In fact, he confirmed that the Real Madrid superstar was leading the voting for a considerable period. Mbappe was leading the Ballon d’Or voting Speaking to L’Equipe after Monday’s ceremony, Garcia confirmed that the battle between Kane and Mbappe was exceptionally close. “The difference was even smaller than between Rodri and Vinicius in 2024, which was 41 points, and that was already a very narrow margin,” he explained. He also explained how Harry Kane overtook him at the last moment. “Mbappe was leading for a long time, but Kane ended up winning. Mbappe has had an extraordinary season. It was incredibly close between Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappe in the battle for first place this year,” he said. Harry Kane pipped Kylian Mbappe to the Ballon d’Or. (Photo by Alex Grimm/Getty Images) Garcia also suggested that Spain’s World Cup success worked against individual candidates, with Rodri and Lamine Yamal splitting votes. The Barcelona youngster eventually finished third, while his team-mate came fourth. For the longest time, it looked like Lamine was in the running for the award. However, judging by Garcia’s words, it looks like it was a two-horse race between Kane and Mbappe, with the former edging it. Real Madrid star has every reason to remain optimistic Mbappe’s individual campaign brought him so close to winning the award even without winning a single trophy for club or country. The French superstar would have almost certainly walked away with the award if Los Blancos had picked up at least one piece of silverware last summer. Mbappe has started the new season in excellent form. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) Ultimately, Kane’s 73 goals for club and country, along with Bayern’s domestic trophies, gave the Englishman an advantage. Mbappe has already started the new season in excellent form, maintaining his ridiculously high goalscoring numbers. He scored twice in Sunday’s 2-1 Clasico victory over Barcelona. Mbappe will know that if he has another good campaign, he could take the final step towards the trophy next year. At 27, the France international is in the prime of his career. His narrow Ballon d’Or defeat might be a bitter pill to swallow, but there will be future chances. Turning his individual excellence into collective trophies will have to be the next step, and it remains to be seen how he fares for Madrid.

item.title: Major Chinese brands drop Mbappé as backlash grows over Mao joke
item.description: A backlash has erupted on Chinese social media over Mbappé's comments on a "Chinese dictator" [Getty Images] Several Chinese brands have dropped French footballer Kylian Mbappé as backlash grew online over alleged comments by him referring to the late Chinese leader Mao Zedong. Mbappé reportedly told French talk show The Bridge a meme "that makes me laugh the most...the one where there's a video of a guy, I think it's a Chinese dictator". As he speaks, a meme appears with his face superimposed on an image resembling Mao. "I use it with my friends all the time," the Real Madrid forward adds, in unverified clips that have been circulating online. Mbappé does not identify Mao by name and the original video is no longer on the show's YouTube channel, but screengrabs have spread on Chinese social media. Mbappé has a significant commercial presence in China [Getty Images] Even China's foreign ministry has weighed in, with spokesperso Lin Jian: "We have noted the relevant reports. Words and deeds that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people will naturally be met with opposition from all sectors of Chinese society." Neither Mbappé nor the The Bridge have commented on this yet. It's unclear when the interview was broadcast but Chinese football forum Dongqiudi drew attention to the comments on Monday night in a statement, saying they were "inappropriate" and "hurt the feelings of Chinese people". A backlash quickly ensued online, with some users criticising Mbappé – who is hugely popular in China and has big endorsements - of "profiting from the Chinese market yet making remarks that offend the Chinese public". "International public figures, in particular, should show greater respect and sensitivity, as national sentiment must never be taken lightly," read another comment on Weibo. Mao founded Communist China in 1949 and ruled through tumultuous decades in the 1960s and 1970s. His attempt at rapid industrialisation, which he called the Great Leap Forward, led to a famine that killed tens of millions. Then came the Cultural Revolution: a violent purge of anyone seen as a threat to Communism, which included Chinese intellectuals, landowners, artists and often rivals within the Party. His death in 1976 brought a new era for China, which began to open its doors to the global economy. Even as the country moved away from Mao's rule, he continued to be hailed by the Chinese Communist Party as a national icon whose legacy was beyond reproach. Given how Mao is regarded to this day in China, the may seem unsurprising to many. The backlash is still growing. item.title: 'I would do it again' - Kaepernick reflects on price of protest, 10 years on
item.description: [Getty Images] "I would absolutely do it again." Ten years on from making the gesture that catapulted him to iconic status, but which he believes led to his exile from the sport he loved, Colin Kaepernick insists he has no regrets. It was September 2016 when NFL star Kaepernick knelt during the US national anthem before a match as a peaceful protest against racial injustice and police brutality. It proved both inspirational and divisive. In his first interview with BBC Sport since then, Kaepernick reflects on his journey; his pride at seeing England footballers take the knee, athlete activism, the relationship between sport and politics, and the price he paid for being a figurehead for the civil rights movement. "I knew the protest could potentially cost me my career," he says. "History shows us…that is a reality for athletes. "We also see this in broader movements, going well beyond costing someone their career, and costing people their lives. We see Malcolm X assassinated, we see MLK [Martin Luther King] assassinated, so the consequences are real." Having initially sat to protest against the plight of black people in the US, Kaepernick first knelt during the Star-Spangled Banner before his San Francisco 49ers team played a pre-season game. It was an act he would repeat before 11 regular-season contests that year. At the time, he said he could not stand up for - and show pride in - a flag "for a country that oppresses black people and people of colour", adding: "This is bigger than football and it would be selfish on my part to look the other way." His stance against racial inequality was seen as heroic by many, inspiring other NFL players to follow suit. But there was also condemnation from those who said it was disrespectful to the military. Those dissenting voices included Donald Trump - then a presidential candidate. Trump described the act as "a terrible thing" and unpatriotic. He even suggested Kaepernick should find another country to live in, adding players who refused to stand for the national anthem should be fired. The NFL said it would fine teams whose players did not stand. Kaepernick opted out of his contract with the 49ers in March 2017, though the club's management later said he would have been released regardless. Despite leading the 49ers to the 2013 Super Bowl, and throwing 16 touchdowns in his final season, one of the most talented quarterbacks in the sport never found a new team. Speaking from New York, Kaepernick says he anticipated the reaction to taking the knee. "What I couldn't have predicted was the people who would show up for me in significant ways, and also the people who worked against me and against the movement," he adds. Kaepernick eventually filed a grievance against NFL team owners, who he believed had conspired not to hire him because of his protests, reaching a financial settlement in 2019. The Milwaukee Brewers are one win away from the first World Series title in franchise history , but Pat Murphy is not about to let his team get comfortable against the Tampa Bay Rays. After Milwaukee’s 10-1 rout in Game 3 on Monday night at Tropicana Field gave the Brewers a commanding 3-0 series lead, Murphy praised his club’s relentlessness while making it clear the job is not done. “I mean, the guys play hard. You know, it’s evident the guys play hard. They just, you know, they don’t give in. And they make every pitch count, and that’s what it takes to win,” Murphy said, via FOX Sports . “And that’s the same thing that Tampa did all year, you know. That team is very, very capable.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Despite being up 3-0, @Brewers Manager Pat Murphy knows the Rays will continue to battle. pic.twitter.com/7RhYkqUvPN — FOX Sports: MLB (@MLBONFOX) October 27, 2026 Murphy acknowledged his team is in a great spot, but he was not ready to call the series. “This is a best-of-seven series. So, it looks like we’re in the driver’s seat, but that doesn’t, you know, it’s baseball. Anything can happen,” Murphy said. “But I like the way we battle.” His team certainly battled on Monday. After taking a 2-0 lead in the third, Milwaukee broke the game open with an eight-run fifth inning , with every run scoring with two outs. Brice Turang’s two-run single was part of a string of seven straight two-out hits, making it one of the biggest innings in World Series history. Jackson Chourio led the way with four hits , while Christian Yelich kept the inning alive by beating out a force play that was overturned on replay. Milwaukee finished with 16 hits. Robert Gasser was just as dominant on the mound. The left-hander tossed six shutout innings and allowed just one hit while facing the minimum. He joined Don Larsen, who threw a perfect game in 1956, as the only pitchers in World Series history to go six-plus innings while facing the minimum. Rays starter Freddy Peralta, meanwhile, failed to get through five innings. The Brewers, now 10-1 this postseason, can clinch the title with a win in Game 4 on Tuesday night. Murphy added that his club has shown it can pounce on any opening. “You give them an inch, sometimes they break through and keep going,” Murphy said. item.title: 'Streets ahead of everyone else!' - Paul Scholes tells Man Utd to ignore 'madman' warning and appoint Antonio Conte
item.description: Antonio Conte Manchester United GFX - Getty/Goal Paul Scholes believes Antonio Conte is the only viable candidate to replace Michael Carrick at Manchester United. The club legend insists the volatile Italian is the perfect manager to shake up the struggling squad and return them to Premier League contention. Mounting pressure at Old Trafford Carrick is facing an increasingly uncertain future at United after a disastrous start to the campaign. The club has endured a dismal run of form, culminating in a heavy 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth at Old Trafford on Sunday. That result leaves United with just one victory in their last eight Premier League outings. Unfortunately for Carrick, the awful performances on the pitch have been matched by growing unrest behind the scenes. Lisandro Martinez has reportedly spoken out against the club’s hierarchy . Meanwhile, club captain Bruno Fernandes has openly aimed criticism at Carrick and his coaching staff , highlighting a deeply fractured dressing room. Scholes identifies the perfect replacement If the club ultimately decides to make a managerial change, Scholes believes Conte is the ideal candidate . When presented with a shortlist including Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann, the United legend was clear on his preference. Speaking on The Good, The Bad and The Football podcast , Scholes admitted the Italian would be a risky but necessary appointment to salvage the season. "You’d have to pick a manager who you think will get us back to being a competitive team for the Premier League," Scholes explained. "Out of them three, Antonio Conte’s the man, but he comes with a big f***ing massive warning. "He’s made noises that he wants to come and I’m pretty sure the club would have spoke to all three of them. I can’t understand why he’d want this job because I don’t think the team’s good enough for him, personally. Emery considered but Conte remains the priority Scholes also suggested Aston Villa manager Unai Emery as a potential solution. He praised the Spaniard for consistently producing excellent results and winning the Europa League, despite frequently losing his best players to transfers. However, the United legend still views Conte as the superior option due to his elite pedigree. "I think Conte’s the best one around," Scholes noted. "When I’m talking best in class and you talk them four, I think Antonio Conte’s miles ahead of all of them. You think Juventus, he went to Napoli and goes and wins the league with them. He’s volatile, I know he’s volatile and might be a bit of a madman, but when you talk about successful managers at top clubs he’s streets ahead. "I don’t care if it’s short term. I don’t care if he’s there 18 months and he gets us challenging for the league, that would be a success. The more and more I think about it, Conte needs to come in and start banging some heads together." item.title: Every Bundesliga Ballon d'Or winner, from Gerd Müller to Harry Kane
item.description: Every Bundesliga Ballon d'Or winner, from Gerd Müller to Harry Kane Harry Kane has won the 2026 Ballon d'Or , becoming the first Bundesliga -based player to claim football's most prestigious individual award since Matthias Sammer in 1996. The Bayern Munich striker scored 73 goals for club and country during the 2025/26 campaign, capping a remarkable season with the game's biggest individual honour. Kane is the seventh player to win the Ballon d'Or while playing for a Bundesliga club, joining a distinguished group that includes Gerd Müller, Franz Beckenbauer and Kevin Keegan . Gerd Muller, Bayern Munich - 1970 Gerd Muller became German football's first Ballon d'Or winner after winning the 1970 award. Der Bomber scored 38 league goals for Bayern Munich to win the European Golden Shoe, before adding 10 goals to win the Golden Boot as West Germany finished third at the 1970 World Cup. Muller failed to win a team trophy, but beat Bobby Moore to the Ballon d'Or. Franz Beckenbauer, Bayern Munich - 1972 and 1976 Franz Beckenbauer was the first German to win multiple Ballon d'Or trophies after success in 1972 and 1976. Beckenbauer's first award came after West Germany won the 1972 European Championship, beating Soviet Union in the final. Beckenbauer had earlier led Bayern Munich to Bundesliga title success. Four years later, Beckenbauer claimed a second Ballon d'Or. Der Kaiser was recognised after Bayern Munich secured a third consecutive European Cup. He was also Ballon d'Or runner-up in 1974 and 1975. Allan Simonsen, Borussia Monchengladbach - 1977 Allan Simonsen remains Denmark's only Ballon d'Or winner, having succeeded Franz Beckenbauer to claim the award in 1977. The forward starred for Borussia Mönchengladbach as the club won the Bundesliga title and reached the European Cup final, scoring against Liverpool in a 3-1 defeat. Simonsen remains the only player to have scored in the finals of the European Cup, UEFA Cup and European Cup Winners' Cup. Kevin Keegan, Hamburg - 1978 and 1979 Kevin Keegan collected the Ballon d'Or in 1978 and 1979 and remains the only English footballer to have won multiple awards. Keegan moved to Hamburg in a record-breaking £500,000 deal in 1977, having helped Liverpool to European Cup success. He won the Ballon d'Or in each of his first two seasons in Germany, after scoring 29 goals in 70 games. His second season saw Hamburg win the Bundesliga for the first time in 19 years. Rummenigge won the 1980 Ballon d'Or after scoring 36 goals in 47 games for Bayern Munich, before earning the Best Player Award as Germany won the 1980 European Championship. item.title: Bruno Fernandes’ position in Ballon d’Or rankings announced
item.description: Bruno Fernandes’ position in Ballon d’Or rankings announced It has certainly been a testing few weeks for Manchester United and their fans. Bruno Fernandes drama The Portuguese star has performed well below his usual standards this season, similar to much of the rest of the team. Fernandes called out the coaching staff after the club’s embarrassing 1-4 defeat to 1907 Como in the Champions League last Wednesday. As a result, he was left out of the starting eleven against AFC Bournemouth on Sunday and did not come on as a substitute, despite United losing the game 0-3. The drama was also intensified as he liked a comment on social media suggesting he was being pushed not to care. Ballon d’Or result In this context, it can be easy to forget the incredible year he enjoyed last season. Fernandes won the Premier League Player of the Season award and broke the league record with 21 assists. He was scintillating as United went on an incredible run of results from January to May, which took them to third in the Premier League table. The club’s official website reported last night, “Bruno Fernandes’s position in the 2026 Ballon d’Or vote has been revealed.” They then announced that he had finished 27th in the rankings. This meant he finished “behind Dayot Upamecano and ahead of Julian Quinones, William Saliba and Sadio Mane.” It is the second time that he has been nominated for the award. His best finish was in 2021, when he finished 21st in the final rankings. This year, Harry Kane was announced as the winner, with Kylian Mbappe coming in second and Lamine Yamal third. After posting 30 points and 16 rebounds in Game 2 and 21 points and 12 rebounds in Game 3, Reese has struggled to find the same offensive rhythm. item.description: Photo by Brianna Bryson/FilmMagic Pat McAfee was not happy with the way the University of Utah mocked him, and went off on them during his show. McAfee was part of the College GameDay crew that travelled to the University of Utah to watch the Utes take on the Houston Cougars. Prior to the event, the University put out a social media post asking fans their thoughts about McAfee, and many of them mocked his antics. Fans believe Pat McAfee is taking University of Utah students’ jokes too seriously Speaking on his show, Pat McAfee expressed his frustration with the University of Utah and how he was treated by the institution while he was hosting College GameDay over the weekend. While he appreciated the opportunity to engage with the students, McAfee didn’t like the fact that the University’s official social media channel shared a video of students mocking him. McAfee said: “I’ve really enjoyed this college football season. Did not enjoy University of Utah. Did not enjoy it. You know why I didn’t like it mostly? Right before I go out there, okay, right before I go out there, I see the University of Utah’s Instagram page, okay?… “They put out a video, can you do an impression of Pat McAfee? And one kid goes, ‘Ah, he’s corny.’ Another kid calls me creepy. “Hey, you, you’re allowed to do what you— the university puts that out? Like, as I’m about to go out and do an infomercial for the place, and then I’m walking in front of thousands of these people, this is how the university feels about it? “It’s an uncomfortable feeling… I’m getting a lot of shrapnel from a lot of places. The university is putting this out. That is something I just had never experienced really in my entire life. So it kind of set me off a little bit. It made me feel a little bit weird, I would say. Made me feel a little bit weird.” Understandably, some fans did not share sympathy for McAfee, as they felt that he was being overly sensitive about some very lighthearted jabs. One fan who was in attendance at College GameDay told Pat: “Pat, it was a good College GameDay. To clarify, I didn’t say you were corny, and nobody said you were creepy.” Another fan added: “This is such a pathetic response to him reacting emotionally when he should not have. To double down on it is crazy.” A third fan who also attended the University of Utah said: “It really was just that video? That’s wild. I thought some other s*** happened for sure. item.title: New-look Scottish rinks eye European curling medals - watch live on BBC
item.description: Grant Hardie and Fay Henderson are eyeing European medals [Getty Images] A glance at the make-up of the Scotland teams going to this week's European Curling Championship tells a story. This time last year, the Scottish women took silver and the men bronze. Yet only three of the 10 curlers who comprised those rinks will be involved in Ostrava over the next six days. So it says something about the strength of curling in Scotland that all of those who travelled to the Czech city on Monday did so with medals in mind. Fay Henderson and Grant Hardie were among those who competed in Finland a year ago. The former as the alternate - or non-playing member - of the women's team and Hardie as deputy to Bruce Mouat in the men's quartet. Now, both have ascended to the skip role and lead new teams, both of which earned their place at the event by winning the Scottish Championships earlier this year in the immediate aftermath of the Winter Olympics. Hardie ended that event on the podium in tears after a second consecutive silver medal. Three months later, he announced he would leave Team Mouat after nine glorious years and become skip of what was Team (Ross) Whyte. Already ranked in the world's top five, they go into these Euros with one aim in mind. "I think it's quite clear for us we want to go there and win it," Hardie told BBC Sport Scotland. "We'll be going in as a top-ranked team but it's a really strong field." While no longer a qualifier for the Worlds, the chance to lay down a marker at the beginning of the Olympics cycle is one Hardie and his team are eager to take. And the feeling is similar for Henderson and her rink. While she stops short of saying gold is the target, a podium place is in her sights. "I've never actually played a game at the Europeans before but have two medals [silver and bronze], which is a bit of a strange feeling," Henderson says. "But I'd love to complete the set. "But, really, we want to show the top teams that we're definitely a force to be reckoned with." [BBC]

item.description: Ezri Konsa scored his first goal for Arsenal in Saturday's win over Everton [Getty Images] When Arsenal confirmed in July that William Saliba would miss an "extended period" with a long-term back issue, you can forgive fans for panicking. The Frenchman has formed a formidable pairing with Gabriel Magalhaes as part of the Gunners' well-drilled backline that conceded just 27 league goals last season as they lifted the Premier League title. Eight games into the new season and Saliba still hasn't featured, but Mikel Arteta's side have conceded the fewest goals in the Premier League as they sit level on points at the summit. That form is testament to the performances of Ezri Konsa, who has stepped up in Saliba's absence and been given his chance to shine. Before Arsenal signed the 29-year-old for £55m from Aston Villa in August, questions were asked. Is it too much money? Do the Gunners need him with Cristhian Mosquera already in the squad? Why bring in Konsa and not a forward? But now, the debate is whether Konsa and Gabriel are the best partnership in world football, not just the Premier League. Arsenal already had seven senior defenders on the books when they signed Konsa. And add in the fact they already had one of the most solid partnerships in world football too, it can be understood why there was confusion about such a big outlay. Arsenal have changed their recruitment strategy, focusing on signings in the peak of their career as they look to capitalise on their win window and continue to lift silverware. Konsa is exactly what they are looking for - in his prime. The defender made 286 appearances for Villa after joining in July 2019 from Brentford and helped them win the Europa League in May, the club's first European trophy since 1982. He has established himself as a first-choice starter for England and started seven of their eight games at the World Cup. His former Aston Villa team-mate, Morgan Rogers - who himself made a big-money move this summer when he joined Chelsea for £117m - said at the World Cup that Konsa does not get the credit he deserves and that he is "one of the best centre-backs in football". Konsa's impressive start Konsa is an imposing figure, quick across the ground, and his aggression in challenges has impressed supporters. Having signed on the opening day of the season, Arteta has praised the way the centre-back has settled in as "unbelievable". item.description: Harry Kane delivered an emotional speech and thanked his wife Katie Goodland after winning the Ballon d’Or on Monday night. England captain and Bayern Munich striker Kane pipped Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal to the most prestigious individual prize in world football, becoming the first Englishman in 25 years to win the award . An emotional Kane, 33, spoke for more than 10 minutes on stage after receiving the award at the London Palladium before thanking his long-term partner, Goodland, mother to his four children. “To my wife, Kate, my best friend,” Kane said. “We've been through ups and downs for sure. You're my biggest supporter. I actually felt like you wanted this more than me myself. “The anxious wait for us to find out, I know it's been horrible for you, here it is - we've done it! You always want the best for me, you sacrifice yourself to help me achieve my dreams, and I know they're your dreams as well, so it wouldn't be possible without you. “This is a trophy that we celebrate, not me. This is me and you, it's all the family, all our close-knit team, so I just want to say thank you, I love you. “Can't wait to enjoy this and celebrate tonight for sure. Love you.” Kane also thanked his wider family, including older brother Charlie and his parents, whom were in attendance on Monday night. “My brother Charlie is here tonight,” he said. It didn't seem that long ago we was kicking a ball around the garden, over the park, watching football, talking football, just football mad. I know you tell me you gave me a lot of your footballing abilities, so thank you very much. I appreciate that. “But to have that love and support from an older brother means the world to me. All those years, the sacrifice you gave me, the support you gave me, the times taking me to training, coming to watch me play all, all around England, all around Germany, no matter where it was, even to this day you're there. “There was never any pressure from you to become a footballer. It was always about working hard. It was always about improving. It was always about learning and all those traits that you have given me have allowed me to be successful and be here tonight. I love you. Thank you very much. “My kids sat home watching, it's definitely past your bedtime, especially as we're [the ceremony] a little later than we hoped. So to Ivy, Vivienne, Louis and Henry. You're the reason I do this. “I don't think you'll fully maybe appreciate bringing this trophy home. I'll bring a few others home, but this one is a special one, so I can't wait to see you and celebrate with you. item.title: Barcelona president Joan Laporta admits Real Madrid Clasico defeat was ‘very tough’
item.description: Barcelona president Joan Laporta admits Real Madrid Clasico defeat was ‘very tough’ Real Madrid secured a 2-1 victory over Barcelona at the Spotify Camp Nou . This has helped Jose Mourinho’s team change the outlook of the title race. Los Blancos travelled to the Spotify Camp Nou six points behind their Catalan rivals. They delivered a statement performance to cut that deficit in half. Barcelona president Joan Laporta has now admitted that the result understandably left the team disappointed. Laporta admits Barcelona are hurting after Clasico defeat While attending Monday’s Ballon d’Or ceremony in London, the Catalan club’s president admitted that the defeat had been particularly painful. “I won’t lie to you, losing the Clasico was very tough,” Laporta said, acknowledging the disappointment of losing to Madrid at home (h/t RM4Arab ). Barcelona had entered Sunday’s encounter with a perfect record in La Liga , winning all nine of their opening matches. Real Madrid outplayed Barcelona in the Clasico. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) Mourinho’s side disrupted that momentum, with Kylian Mbappe scoring twice, the second time late in the game, to seal the victory. Raphinha had briefly restored parity for Barcelona in the second half, but Jose Mourinho’s tactics ensured Los Blancos returned with all three points. Laporta also acknowledged that Barça had struggled to impose their usual style of play. However, he backed Hansi Flick and the team going forward. Real Madrid deliver an important psychological blow For Madrid, Laporta’s words underline that Sunday’s result goes beyond just three points in the league table. Mourinho’s team approached the contest with a resolute defensive structure . This limited Barça ‘s attacking opportunities. Jose Mourinho will want his team to keep getting more consistent in the coming weeks. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) The performance was arguably Madrid’s best so far under Mourinho, and winning at the Camp Nou against a dominant Barça side is a sign of improvement for Los Blancos . The victory might also have handed a psychological boost to the Catalan side, who were flying high before the start of the week. Madrid should look to use this situation to push on and try to close the three-point gap if Barça drop any more points. Barça clearly did not see what was coming from Jose Mourinho’s men on Sunday, and it remains to be seen how the La Liga title race pans out from here.

item.description: Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni provided an injury update on banged up running back Saquon Barkley. Getty The Philadelphia Eagles lost a fifth consecutive game Monday night, falling to the Dallas Cowboys 38-21. The 2026 season is quickly becoming a lost season for the Eagles, but it’s rather clear running back Saquon Barkley isn’t giving up just yet. Barkley played despite obviously dealing with a leg injury throughout the night. The running back shared with reporters he re-injured his hamstring and tweaked his back on the first play of the game. Barkley fought through the injuries to provide what production he could. The All-Pro ran for 62 yards and a touchdown. It was a typical great player delivering what he could to try and provide his struggling team a spark. item.title: KIMI ANTONELLI IS ONE RACE FROM F1 HISTORY! The Mexican Grand Prix Could Crown a New World Champion
item.description: May 24, 2026; Montreal, Quebec, CANADA; Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli (12) celebrates his win during the Lenovo Grand Prix Du Canada at Circuit Gilles-Villeneuve. Mandatory Credit: Eric Bolte-Imagn Images Formula 1 could be on the verge of witnessing history. Kimi Antonelli won the United States Grand Prix in Austin on Oct. 25, extending his championship lead and putting himself within touching distance of his first world title. Now, the spotlight shifts to Mexico City. The question is no longer whether the Mercedes driver has championship potential. It is whether anyone can stop him from becoming the youngest Formula 1 world champion in history. The Championship Is Antonelli’s to Lose Antonelli leads the standings with 365 points, 123 ahead of teammate George Russell and 124 clear of Lewis Hamilton. With only five rounds remaining after Austin, the mathematics are becoming increasingly difficult for his rivals. The 20-year-old can clinch the championship at the Mexican Grand Prix on Nov. 1 by finishing ninth or better. He could also seal the title if neither Russell nor Hamilton wins the race. That is an extraordinary position for a driver still in only his second Formula 1 season. Antonelli has already won nine Grands Prix this year. His latest victory in Austin came after he started from pole position and finished more than 13 seconds ahead of Charles Leclerc. Who Can Actually Stop Him? Russell and Hamilton remain the only drivers mathematically capable of catching Antonelli. That is a remarkable development in a season that once featured a much wider championship conversation. Max Verstappen, Charles Leclerc and other contenders have been eliminated from title contention. Antonelli’s advantage is substantial, but the championship is not officially over yet. A difficult weekend in Mexico could delay the celebrations. Mercedes also has an opportunity to secure the constructors’ championship, adding another potential milestone to an already enormous weekend. A New Era of Formula 1? Hamilton became a global superstar by winning seven world championships. Verstappen built a dominant run of his own. Now, Antonelli is on the verge of announcing himself as the sport’s next defining champion. Winning a title at 20 would be a historic achievement. Doing it in just his second season would make the accomplishment even more remarkable. The Mexican Grand Prix could become a coronation — or the opening of one final chapter of suspense. F1 fans, is Kimi Antonelli already the face of the sport’s future? Or does he need to win multiple championships before earning that label?

item.description: The basketball world slams the WNBA over a possible practice court championship celebration after ESPN insider Ramona Shelburne reveals the potential plan. The WNBA is drawing criticism after ESPN insider Ramona Shelburne reported Monday that the championship celebration could be moved to a practice court if the Golden State Valkyries win the title in Game 6. The possibility stems from a scheduling conflict at Atlanta’s State Farm Arena, where an NBA game is set for later that day. Shelburne’s report on “NBA Today” prompted sharp reactions from the basketball world. Basketball Community Slams WNBA Over Potential Practice Court Celebration Game 6 of the WNBA Finals is scheduled for Thursday at 12:30 p.m. ET, with the Atlanta Hawks hosting the Cleveland Cavaliers at State Farm Arena at 8 p.m. The tight turnaround between the two games has raised concerns about how much time the arena will have to accommodate both events. Shelburne addressed the scheduling issue: “That championship celebration may not actually be on that court,” she said . “I’ve heard there are discussions about whether there’s enough time to turn the arena over in time for the fans to celebrate on the court. It could be moved to like a practice court.” The possibility of moving the ceremony away from the main court drew criticism from across the basketball world. Celtics writer Noa Dalzell posted , “This is ridiculous.” One WNBA observer raised concerns about what the arrangement could mean for the players, writing, “This is so embarrasing just potentially ruining a championship celebration.” Golden State leads the best-of-seven series 3-2 after defeating Atlanta 64-55 in Game 5 on Monday. The Valkyries can secure their first championship with another victory Thursday, while the Dream must win to force Game 7.
